nodes.excerpt: Opt-in, and unusual: --sandbox <profile> makes the binary confine its whole process at startup, before the agent boots — Landlock on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS, a bubblewrap re-exec for read-deny mounts. Profiles run workspace -> read-only -> strict; child-process network blocking is seccomp-based and a no-op on macOS. Off by default: without the flag, commands run unconfined.

nodes.excerpt: An explicit loop {} in process_conversation_turn_inner, emitting LoopStarted each iteration and making exactly one sampler round-trip per pass. A response with no tool calls ends the turn. There is no default turn cap — the real brake is the stationarity guard: order-insensitive step hashes, a nudge at 8 identical steps (4 for reads/plan calls), a hard stop at 12 (8), and true no-op runs stopped at 4.

nodes.excerpt: The model client speaks three wire formats — Chat Completions, Messages, Responses — chosen per catalog entry. Session/OAuth traffic is proxied through cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1; an API key goes to api.x.ai/v1. BYOK custom models carry their own base URL, key, headers, and context window. A server-delivered doom-loop policy (the x-grok-doom-loop-check header) is parsed and enforced client-side, layered over the local guard.

nodes.excerpt: Tools are rows in a registry, in three toolsets — native, a concise variant, and a hashline variant — plus in-tree ports of tool implementations from openai/codex and sst/opencode, disclosed in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES. MCP tools join the same registry and pass through the same permission pipeline as built-ins; subagents spawn through the task tool, optionally in a fresh git worktree.

nodes.excerpt: Six modes (default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan) over a fixed pipeline: PreToolUse hooks -> rules (deny > ask > allow) -> remembered per-project grants -> built-in read-only auto-approvals, evaluated per segment with execution-smuggling exceptions -> the mode's policy. Auto mode replaces the prompt with an LLM transcript classifier. Administrators can lock always-approve off via requirements.toml.

nodes.excerpt: When trace upload is on, each completed turn packages its messages and full prompt text, chat_history.jsonl, the turn's permission events, and git root/remote metadata — via a disk-spilling queue to a deployment bucket, the cli-chat-proxy, or S3. In this tree the gates default closed: telemetry mode defaults to Disabled, and the coding-data opt-out defaults to opted-out until the server says otherwise. Spilled uploads are purged at startup if collection is disabled.

Its archive upload is separately gated on the session registry, and the skip is recorded in the turn's manifest.

nodes.excerpt: One precedence shape decides nearly everything: requirements pin -> environment -> local config -> remote settings -> built-in default. At startup the client fetches remote settings (GET /v1/settings on the cli-chat-proxy); the payload can enable features, set the telemetry mode, turn trace upload on, enable the session registry, and carry a server-decided consent notice. Managed (enterprise) configuration rides the same machinery.
